H-01.claim: Unary minus binds tighter than ^, so =-2^2 is 4 (as in Excel).

H-03.claim: Equality compares at 15 significant digits, so =0.1+0.2=0.3 is TRUE.

H-04.claim: A result within 15 significant digits of zero snaps to 0, e.g. (0.1+0.2)-0.3.

H-05.claim: ROUND, ROUNDUP, ROUNDDOWN, MROUND and TRUNC work on the 15-significant-digit decimal string, rounding half away from zero (ROUND(1.005,2) = 1.01).

H-06.claim: Sheets has no 1900 leap-year bug: serial 60 is 1900-02-28 and DATE(1900,2,29) is 1900-03-01.

H-07.claim: Negative serials are dates before 1899-12-30 (or an error); TEXT/YEAR of a negative serial.

H-08.claim: DATE adds 1900 to a year in 0..1899; a year below 0 or at least 10000 is #NUM!.

H-09.claim: Approximate VLOOKUP/MATCH/LOOKUP over an unsorted column runs a binary search, and the result follows that search.

H-10.claim: AND and OR do NOT short-circuit: an error in a later argument still surfaces.

H-11.claim: A multi-cell range or array in a scalar context without ARRAYFORMULA takes its first element (or errors).

H-12.claim: Aggregates coerce LITERAL text and boolean arguments (SUM(1,"2",TRUE) = 4) but skip them inside ranges.

H-13.claim: Mixed types order as number < text < boolean in comparisons.

H-14.claim: Text comparison and lookup are case-insensitive, including non-ASCII letters.

H-15.claim: LEN, LEFT and MID count UTF-16 code units, so an emoji outside the BMP is 2.

H-16.claim: #NULL! and #ERROR! exist as Sheets error values with ERROR.TYPE codes.

H-17.claim: The xlsx Sheets exports keeps full double precision (17 significant digits).

H-18.claim: The text "TRUE" / "FALSE" (any case) coerces to a boolean in IF/AND/OR/NOT; other text is #VALUE!.

H-19.claim: An empty cell compares as 0 against a number and as "" against text.

H-20.claim: When several arguments are errors, the first in evaluation order wins.

H-21.claim: Cell references are accepted inside array literals ({TRUE,A1}), as MOIC's SUMPRODUCT form needs.

H-22.claim: INDEX with a row past the range is #REF! (MOIC expects #REF!; Sheets may say #NUM!).

H-23.claim: Number-to-text (& and text functions) uses the 15-significant-digit general form (1/3 -> 0.333333333333333).

H-24.claim: Numeric text coerces in arithmetic: "5%" -> 0.05, date-like text -> serial, surrounding spaces allowed; thousands separators and currency symbols are a question.

H-25.claim: An open range (B:B) is sized by the populated extent of the inputs (the engine) -- Sheets sizes it by the grid, so ROWS(B:B) is a known divergence candidate.

H-26.claim: Two-digit years in date TEXT ("1/1/29", "1/1/30") follow a fixed pivot in Sheets.

H-27.claim: INDEX with an omitted row argument (INDEX(r,,1)) returns the whole column, as MOIC's XLOOKUP form needs.

H-28.claim: Criteria strings are a closed grammar: "=SUM(A1)" means equality with the TEXT SUM(A1), and "==1+1" matches the text =1+1.

H-29.claim: MOD takes the sign of the divisor (not fmod's sign of the dividend).

H-30.claim: CEILING and FLOOR with a positive number and negative factor (or the reverse) follow Sheets, not Excel's #NUM!.

H-31.claim: IFERROR with value_if_error omitted returns an empty string.

H-33.claim: SUMPRODUCT over arrays of different sizes is an error, not #N/A padding.

H-34.claim: A text value longer than 50,000 characters is an error.

H-35.claim: The TYPE of an error value is 16 and the TYPE of an array literal is 64.
